one_line_thesis: ETHA is a passive iShares spot-ether trust: return is ether beta minus a 0.25% sponsor fee and any premium or discount to net asset value at purchase, not operating owner cash flow.

deep_dive.executive_summary: At $20.37 (Yahoo close 2026-10-01), the base case implies about 3.9% per year over seven years if filed net asset value per share compounds with 8% per year ether growth and a 0.25% sponsor fee, holding share count flat for illustration. The share price already sits roughly 28% above the last published net asset value per share ($15.87 at March 31, 2026), so much of the ether upside is priced in. ETHA is not an operating compounder: economics are look-through ether minus fees. Marvin proposes watch until premium or discount to net asset value and the ether path fit the allocator mandate. industry.structure: U.S. spot ether exchange-traded products compete on fees, liquidity, and authorized-participant creation/redemption efficiency. BlackRock iShares ETHA is one of several SEC-registered trusts holding physical ether with NASDAQ-listed shares.
industry.share_shift: 2025 saw rapid asset gathering into spot crypto exchange-traded products; ETHA grew from roughly $3.6B to $10.3B net asset value in FY2025 before Q1 2026 drawdown and net redemptions.
industry.trend: Ether price volatility, regulatory clarity debates, and Ethereum network upgrades (protocol changes) remain the dominant drivers; product economics are passive fee drag plus tracking basis versus spot ether.
